title: Trust but Verify: Evidence in Science
text:
Scientific research depends on evidence that can be reproduced by other researchers. When an experiment yields results that cannot be repeated, the original claim becomes doubtful, even if it was initially published in a respected journal. For this reason, many journals now require authors to share their raw data and methods in detail. Such transparency allows independent teams to examine whether the conclusions genuinely follow from the observations.

The so-called replication crisis has led some scientists to rethink how studies are designed and analysed. Small sample sizes, flexible statistical methods and the pressure to publish striking findings have all been blamed for producing misleading results. Consequently, a growing number of researchers now register their hypotheses before collecting data. Although this practice does not eliminate error, it makes it harder to adjust conclusions after the results are known.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what happens when an experiment's results cannot be repeated?
options: The claim becomes doubtful, even if it was published in a respected journal
The journal automatically publishes a correction
The researchers receive a larger research grant
The experiment is considered a complete success

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what has been blamed for producing misleading results?
options: Small sample sizes, flexible statistics and pressure to publish
A lack of funding for laboratory equipment
Researchers who share their raw data

questions.text: Why might registering hypotheses before collecting data be useful?
options: It guarantees that the results will be positive
It removes the need for statistical analysis
It makes it harder to change conclusions after seeing the results
It allows researchers to avoid peer review

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's attitude toward the replication crisis?
options: They believe science is fundamentally unreliable
They think the problem is serious but is being addressed
They consider the crisis exaggerated and unimportant
They are indifferent to whether results can be reproduced

vocabulary.definition: made again by other researchers to check that the result is the same
not certain or not likely to be true
the quality of sharing information openly so others can check it
giving a wrong impression of what is true

paragraph_translations: Badania naukowe opierają się na dowodach, które mogą zostać odtworzone przez innych badaczy. Gdy wyników eksperymentu nie da się powtórzyć, pierwotne twierdzenie staje się wątpliwe, nawet jeśli zostało wstępnie opublikowane w renomowanym czasopiśmie. Z tego powodu wiele czasopism wymaga teraz, by autorzy szczegółowo udostępniali surowe dane i metody. Taka przejrzystość pozwala niezależnym zespołom sprawdzić, czy wnioski rzeczywiście wynikają z obserwacji.

Tak zwany kryzys replikacji skłonił niektórych naukowców do przemyślenia sposobu projektowania i analizowania badań. Małe próby badawcze, elastyczne metody statystyczne oraz presja na publikowanie uderzających odkryć zostały obwinione o tworzenie mylących wyników. W konsekwencji coraz więcej badaczy rejestruje swoje hipotezy, zanim zbierze dane. Choć ta praktyka nie eliminuje błędów, utrudnia zmienianie wniosków po poznaniu wyników.
